evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), 50 m NE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2015 (fire V50256), 30 m NW: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 12 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 70 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of North Cowichan, about 102 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.54249, -123.8466, pull off on Carlson Point Rd (gravel road). Map links below.

Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-5, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
